framework.primary_law: Layered CAC regulations: Recommendation Algorithms (2022), Deep Synthesis (2023), Generative AI Interim Measures (2023), AI-Generated Content Labelling Measures (2025)
framework.enforcing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) with MIIT, MPS and others
framework.max_penalty: Under PIPL: up to RMB 50 million or 5% of annual revenue; criminal liability for serious offences
framework.geographic_scope: Services offered to the public in mainland China, including foreign providers.

research.summary: China regulates AI through targeted administrative rules rather than one comprehensive statute: recommendation algorithms (in force March 2022), deep synthesis (January 2023), generative AI (15 August 2023) and mandatory explicit and implicit labelling of AI-generated content from 1 September 2025. Providers with public opinion influence must complete security assessments and filings before launch. Ethics review measures (December 2023) cover AI research enterprises.

key_provisions.title: Generative AI Interim Measures
key_provisions.description: Providers must respect socialist core values, use lawful training data, and complete security assessment and filing if they can influence public opinion.

key_provisions.title: AI content labelling
key_provisions.description: Explicit and implicit labels are required on AI-generated and synthetic content from 1 September 2025.

key_provisions.title: Science and technology ethics review
key_provisions.description: Ethics review for enterprises engaged in AI and similar activities (trial measures, 1 December 2023).

cross_jurisdiction_tensions.tension: Content-control and filing requirements in China conflict with US free-speech-oriented and export-control approaches; firms face incompatible compliance demands.

safety_risk_management.rationale: Security assessments and filing before launch; national standards on training data security from 1 November 2025.

privacy_data_protection.rationale: PIPL and data security laws apply; state access is broad.

human_oversight.rationale: Oversight is exercised by the state, with limited individual oversight rights.

transparency.rationale: Mandatory explicit and implicit labelling of synthetic content.

accountability.rationale: Clear regulator accountability and penalties, but accountability to individuals is limited.

fairness_non_discrimination.rationale: Fairness duties are limited and tied to content rules.

environmental_sustainability.rationale: Data centre efficiency and renewable steering targets exist, but not AI-specific ethics duties.

access_to_remedy.rationale: Complaint routes exist but independent redress is limited.

gaps_and_weaknesses: No comprehensive AI statute; legal definition of AI is unclear.
State-aligned content rules sit alongside rights protections.
research.monitor_notes: Check status of any draft comprehensive AI law, the Cybersecurity Law amendment and the AI Safety Governance Framework; none were verified in the sources used. Scores are provisional AI-drafted judgements against the AIETHOS rubric and reflect protections currently in force.

citizen.one_line: In China the state sets the rules on AI: AI content must be labelled and companies must file their systems with regulators.
citizen.what_changed: Since 1 September 2025, AI-generated images, video, audio and text must carry visible and hidden labels. Public-facing generative AI services must pass a security review.
citizen.who_is_protected: People using AI services in mainland China, within the limits of state content rules.
who_is_not_protected: People whose speech or data is covered by state security and content provisions

your_rights.how_to_invoke: Report unlabelled content to the platform or the CAC reporting channel.

your_rights.what_it_means: PIPL gives rights over personal data used by AI services.
your_rights.how_to_invoke: Request access, correction or deletion from the service provider.

citizen.plain_language_summary: China requires labelling and filing for AI, and the government decides what AI may say. Individual rights exist but are limited.

jargon_buster.Filing (备案): A required registration of an AI service with regulators before launch.
jargon_buster.Deep synthesis: AI that generates or alters faces, voices, text or video.
